afterJson.description: Rover Pipeline LLC is a large-scale interstate natural gas transmission system connecting Marcellus and Utica production in Pennsylvania and West Virginia with demand markets across Ohio, Michigan and the broader Midwest. The approximately 700-to-713-mile system has 3.425 Bcf/d of transportation capacity, is substantially contracted under long-term agreements and is operated by an Energy Transfer affiliate. The canonical PortCo is Rover Pipeline LLC; ET Rover Pipeline LLC, BCP Renaissance entities and Traverse Midstream Partners are ownership vehicles, while pipeline segments, interconnects and the separately owned Ohio River System are outside the Rover company boundary. Affiliates of investment funds managed by Alinda Capital Partners and Universities Superannuation Scheme acquired APM Terminals Virginia and renamed the terminal owner Virginia International Gateway.
Astatine reports that its Alinda Infrastructure Fund II investment in Virginia International Gateway was exited in 2019; the manager separately retains an Active VIG profile.

afterJson.description: Virginia International Gateway is the private owner of the highly automated VIG marine container terminal in Portsmouth, Virginia. The terminal handles containerized cargo for ocean carriers, beneficial cargo owners, railroads, motor carriers and regional supply chains; Astatine describes approximately 2 million TEU of annual throughput capacity. Virginia International Gateway, Inc. owns the terminal, the Virginia Port Authority leases it under a long-term facilities lease, and the authority's Virginia International Terminals subsidiary operates it. The facility opened in 2007 as APM Terminals Virginia. Affiliates of Alinda-managed funds and USS acquired it in August 2014 and renamed it VIG. Astatine now lists one VIG profile as Active and a separate Fund II investment as exited in 2019. The Virginia Port Authority's August 2025 final official statement identifies USS and PSP as the current underlying owners, supporting an active Astatine manager attribution and an active PSP direct-owner association while preserving the realized Fund II period. The active Astatine fund or managed-account vehicle, manager-level stake and entry date, plus PSP's entry date and percentage, are not publicly disclosed. No later full sale, signed pending exit or transfer of terminal title to the port authority was identified through August 18, 2026. APM Terminals Virginia is the predecessor name; VPA, VIT, lease interests, bonds, cranes and expansion projects are not separate PortCos.

beforeJson.description: DataBank provides colocation, interconnection, and managed infrastructure services for enterprise, cloud, and artificial-intelligence workloads. Its customers include enterprises, hyperscale users, and network counterparties that require data-center capacity, connectivity, and related managed services across multiple U.S. markets. The operating model is asset-heavy because the business owns and operates data-center facilities and critical power and cooling infrastructure, with revenues generated through long-term capacity, colocation, and service contracts. AustralianSuper describes the platform as one of the larger North American data-center operators, and public disclosures in 2024 referenced more than 65 data centers across 27 key markets and a build-out plan exceeding 850 MW of additional capacity. DataBank was founded in 2005, DigitalBridge has been a long-term sponsor since 2016, and AustralianSuper became a significant minority owner through the 2024 equity raise.

Digital Bridge acquired DataBank from Avista Capital Partners with TIAA, Allstate Investments and The Edgewater Funds, launching its first data-center platform.

Colony Capital purchased $185 million of secondary DataBank interests from Edgewater and Allstate; Edgewater exited, Allstate retained half of its prior interest and the Nuveen-branded TIAA investment continued.

afterJson.description: DataBank Holdings, Ltd. operates a nationwide digital-infrastructure platform providing colocation, interconnection, cloud, storage, managed security and compliance services to enterprise, cloud, content and technology customers. Founded in Dallas in 2005, DataBank was acquired from Avista by a DigitalBridge-led group in July 2016 and has since expanded through acquisitions, development and multiple recapitalizations. DataBank reported more than 70 data centers in more than 25 markets, 20 interconnection hubs, more than 2,200 customers and more than $1 billion of revenue in May 2026. The current manager-universe ownership roster is DigitalBridge, Swiss Life Asset Managers, IMCO, AustralianSuper, Northleaf Capital Partners, Ardian and CBRE Investment Management. DigitalBridge disclosed a 7.8% continuing stake after the January 2025 secondary. TIAA's Real Estate Account separately disclosed a 14.8% beneficial stake through DigitalBridge Zeus vehicles; DataBank brands that relationship as Nuveen, but it is not evidenced as a Nuveen Infrastructure investment. EDF Invest and TJC are also current investors outside the supplied manager universe. Individual data centers, campuses, interconnection hubs and acquired operating assets remain within the single DataBank platform boundary. No later full sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026.

canonicalCompany.description: Transurban Chesapeake owns the 495, 95, and 395 Express Lanes system serving the greater Washington, D.C. region. Its customers are passenger and commercial motorists that pay variable tolls for managed-lane access and travel-time reliability. The platform is asset-heavy and concession-based because value depends on long-dated toll-road rights, lane assets, traffic demand, and ongoing operations. CPP Investments disclosed in 2020 that it acquired a 15% interest, and subsequent Transurban investor materials show a current ownership split of 50% Transurban, 25% AustralianSuper, 15% CPP Investments, and 10% UniSuper. The asset base remains a core managed-lanes platform in Virginia, Maryland, and the District of Columbia.

beforeJson.description: Bluepoint Wind is an offshore wind development project planned in federal waters serving the New York and New Jersey markets. The project is intended to supply utility-scale renewable power into state-led offshore wind procurement programs and related power markets. Its operating model is asset-heavy and development-led, with value creation tied to permitting, interconnection, construction, and long-term contracted offtake rather than merchant-only exposure. Public project materials state that the lease area is located about 38 nautical miles off New York and 53 nautical miles off New Jersey and is designed for up to 2.4 GW of generation capacity. The project is owned by a partnership between Ocean Winds and Global Infrastructure Partners. The Bluepoint Wind name and public project branding were introduced in 2022 as the sponsors advanced the project in the Northeast U.S. offshore wind market.

Vineyard Northeast is the lease and project identity for OCS-A 0522, whose current lessee is Vineyard Northeast LLC; Vineyard Wind 2 is a proposed project of up to 1.2 GW inside that lease, not a separate manager-level company. A 50/50 Avangrid and CIP joint venture won the lease in 2018 and it became effective on April 1, 2019. On January 10, 2022, a CI IV vehicle acquired Avangrid's interest and obtained 100% of the lease rights. Massachusetts provisionally selected 800 MW in September 2024, but Vineyard Offshore withdrew the bid on December 20, 2024 after Connecticut made no offshore-wind selection. The lease remains active, while FAST-41 permitting is paused to April 1, 2027; no PPA, FID, financing close, construction start, lease surrender, sale, CIP exit or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026. Vineyard Northeast, Vineyard Wind 2, Excelsior Wind and their lease SPVs are consolidated beneath this one platform record; Vineyard Wind 1 remains distinct.

afterJson.description: Autopista Arco Norte, S.A. de C.V., commonly known as Arco Norte, operates a 223-kilometer federal user-pay toll road across the State of Mexico, Hidalgo, Tlaxcala and Puebla. The concession was granted on December 21, 2005 and is scheduled to expire on December 20, 2065. IDEAL contributed its 99% Arco Norte interest to Promotora Punta Cometa, S.A. de C.V. in the partnership that closed on December 22, 2016; at close, CPP Investments held 29% of that vehicle and Ontario Teachers' held 20%, alongside IDEAL and a small Inbursa affiliate interest. Later FIDEAL restructuring changed the direct capitalization beneath the road, so current manager look-through percentages are not publicly disclosed and the 2016 percentages should not be presented as direct concessionaire stakes. Ontario Teachers' continues to list Arco Norte separately from IDEAL, supporting treatment as its own manager-level infrastructure holding. No manager exit, concession transfer, termination or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026. Promotora Punta Cometa is the upstream holding vehicle; IDEAL Group and Pacifico Sur remain separate investments.

canonicalCompany.description: Caturus is an integrated natural gas and LNG platform that combines upstream gas production with associated midstream and export infrastructure. Its end markets include LNG buyers, gas marketers, and downstream customers seeking low-emission U.S. natural gas supply linked to export capacity. The operating model is asset-heavy and integrated, spanning production, gathering and related infrastructure, and an LNG export project through Commonwealth LNG rather than a pure asset-light marketing model. Public materials state that the platform had crossed the 600 MMcfe per day threshold by August 2025 and targets 3 Bcfe per day over time, while also advancing the 9.5 mtpa Commonwealth LNG project. Kimmeridge first publicly closed development-capital funding for Commonwealth LNG in August 2023, closed a follow-on control investment in June 2024, and later rebranded SoTex HoldCo as Caturus in August 2025 when Mubadala Energy closed a strategic investment for a 24.1% equity stake.

afterJson.description: Caturus is an integrated U.S. natural-gas and LNG platform whose legal parent is Caturus Holdco, LLC, renamed from SoTex HoldCo in August 2025. The platform combines Caturus Energy's Texas upstream production with the controlled 9.5 mtpa Commonwealth LNG export project in Cameron Parish, Louisiana. After the May 14, 2026 CPP Investments closing, regulatory filings support a direct governance cap table of 52.6% Kimmeridge-managed interests, 24.1% Mubadala, 22.8% CPP Investments and 0.5% Caturus management. CPP also has a disclosed economic look-through through Kimmeridge-managed funds, but that indirect interest carries no additional governance and public CPP percentages use a different aggregation basis; the 22.8% direct interest is therefore used for the ownership row. Kimmeridge's exact fund allocation and CPP's primary-versus-secondary mix are not publicly disclosed. Caturus reported more than 1 Bcfe per day of net production across approximately 280,000 net acres after the Galvan Ranch acquisition, while Commonwealth LNG reached FID and closed project financing in May 2026. Caturus Energy and Commonwealth LNG are subordinate operating subsidiaries/projects, not separate manager-level PortCos, and project financiers are not parent owners. No later platform sale, owner exit, cancellation or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

retiredCompanies.description: Beanfield Technologies owns and operates metro fiber broadband and enterprise connectivity infrastructure in Canada. The company serves commercial buildings, residential developments, and enterprise customers with fiber-based internet, transport, and related telecom services. Its model is asset-heavy and facilities-based, with the company building, owning, and maintaining its own network rather than relying mainly on resale arrangements. Public disclosures tied to OMERS' investment state that Beanfield's network spans about 4,000 kilometers and serves roughly 4,000 commercial buildings and 170,000 residential units, primarily in Toronto, Vancouver, and Montreal. Beanfield was founded in 1988, DigitalBridge acquired the business in 2019, and OMERS Infrastructure made a strategic investment in the parent entity in 2023.

beforeJson.description: Crown Castle Small Cells Solutions comprises Crown Castle's small-cell and venue communications infrastructure business in the United States. It serves mobile network operators and venue customers that require densification and in-building or outdoor wireless connectivity assets. The business is asset-heavy and lease-based because it consists of physical small-cell, fiber-connected, and venue communications infrastructure. Public transaction materials describe the business as part of Crown Castle's fiber segment and note that it includes the company's small-cell and venue assets. EQT Active Core Infrastructure signed a definitive agreement in March 2025 to acquire the business, and Crown Castle announced the completed sale of its Small Cell business to Arium Networks, an EQT Active Core Infrastructure fund company, on May 1, 2026.

The facility connects marine, rail, truck and pipeline logistics and has 1,518,200 barrels of operator-listed storage capacity. It handles renewable fuels, sustainable-aviation-fuel components and blends, biodiesel, aviation gasoline, distillates and crude oil during a permitted transition that requires crude handling and storage to end by October 2027. Warburg Pincus and Kelso & Company acquired the broader Zenith Energy U.S. platform in 2017 and remain the current sponsors while their signed sale of the Portland terminal is pending. The Portland terminal is counted as a standalone PortCo; its tanks, docks, pipeline, racks and conversion projects remain subordinate assets.

The operating model is asset-heavy and development-to-ownership because the business originates, finances, builds, and operates physical generation and storage assets with a mix of contracted and market-based revenues. Public disclosures describe a portfolio concentrated in California with additional assets in Texas and New York, including roughly 3.8 GW of operating capacity and 5.1 GWh of storage across about 30 sites, plus a development pipeline exceeding 12 GW. Terra-Gen was formed in 2007, Igneo made its initial investment through Global Diversified Infrastructure Fund (GDIF) in December 2020, and Masdar closed the acquisition of a 50 percent stake in October 2024 while Igneo retained its 50 percent interest.

canonicalCompany.description: CRCHUM is a hospital research facility affiliated with the Université de Montréal and the CHUM health system. The center supports basic, clinical, and population-health research rather than a commercial end market, making it a social infrastructure asset with institutional users and long-term public-sector relevance. Its model is asset-heavy and facility-based, with public materials describing a 70,000-square-meter building that hosts more than 1,700 people, including around 450 researchers and more than 400 graduate students and postdoctoral fellows. Operations are concentrated in Montréal within Quebec's academic and healthcare research ecosystem. CRCHUM was founded in 1996, construction of the current facility began in 2010, the building opened in 2013, and Meridiam is the long-term infrastructure investor associated with the project.

beforeJson.description: Altán Redes operates Mexico's shared wholesale mobile network, Red Compartida. Its customers are mobile network operators, MVNOs, enterprises, and public-sector users that buy wholesale capacity rather than retail subscribers, and the business runs an asset-heavy national wireless infrastructure platform. Public company and government sources describe the network as a 4.5G LTE wholesale system with population coverage above 94% as of mid-2024, although other later public reports cite lower figures using different measures. Altán was created to deploy and operate the Red Compartida under a long-term public-private partnership and received its concession in 2017. Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners publicly lists Altán as a portfolio investment from March 2017, but reviewed sources also show a later government-led financial restructuring and state participation. Because the current sponsor-level ownership structure after that restructuring is not clearly disclosed in the public sources reviewed, ownership details are recorded as not publicly disclosed.

canonicalCompany.description: CSV Midstream develops, owns, and operates natural gas and natural gas liquids processing infrastructure in Alberta's Montney region. Its customers are upstream producers that require gas processing, compression, gathering, and related midstream services under contracted arrangements. The business follows an asset-heavy model centered on gas plants, compressor stations, and associated facilities rather than a pure marketing or advisory approach. Public materials state that CSV has grown from a single gas plant in 2019 to a network of six plants serving Grande Prairie, Grande Cache, and surrounding areas of northern Alberta. Northleaf acquired 100% of CSV in June 2019, including the Resthaven gas processing facility and Pipestone South compressor station, and has remained the company's disclosed infrastructure sponsor.

The operating model is asset heavy and rate regulated, with cash flows derived from utility service rather than merchant water sales. The company states that it was founded in 2016 and has pursued a consolidation strategy focused on smaller-scale regulated utility systems. Ridgewood acquired the platform in 2017, making it one of the earlier utility investments in the firm's current portfolio. The business remains part of Ridgewood's water infrastructure strategy.

beforeJson.description: Valley Cold Storage & Transportation provides temperature-controlled warehousing and related logistics services in southern New Mexico. Public company materials describe two strategically located facilities along the I-10 and I-25 corridors serving southern New Mexico, northern Mexico, and west Texas. Valley Cold's website identifies 2020 as the year of the current operating platform's launch, and Ridgewood Infrastructure acquired the company in 2024.

Its model is asset-heavy and facilities-based, with the company building, owning, and maintaining its own network rather than relying mainly on resale arrangements. Public disclosures tied to OMERS' investment state that Beanfield's network spans about 4,000 kilometers and serves roughly 4,000 commercial buildings and 170,000 residential units, primarily in Toronto, Vancouver, and Montreal. Beanfield was founded in 1988, DigitalBridge acquired the business in 2019, and OMERS Infrastructure made a strategic investment in the parent entity in 2023.

retiredCompanyBeforeImages.description: CleanCapital C&I Solar SPVs are project vehicles used to own and finance distributed clean energy assets in the United States. Their end markets are commercial, industrial, and distributed-generation customers that require operating solar assets and related project finance structures. The model is asset-heavy and contracted, with value supported by operating solar projects and associated long-term power arrangements. Public materials show that Generate and CleanCapital announced a partnership in 2017 focused on acquiring approximately US$300 million of operating clean energy assets, with an initial emphasis on distributed solar. The reviewed materials did not disclose the current ownership percentages within individual SPVs or portfolio-level revenue. The relationship formed part of the early build-out of Generate's distributed generation investment activity, while CleanCapital later expanded into a broader U.S. solar and storage owner-operator platform.

retiredCompanyBeforeImages.description: The CHUM Research Centre, or CRCHUM, is a healthcare public-private partnership asset in Montreal. The project serves the Centre hospitalier de l'Université de Montréal modernization program and supports hospital and research functions for the public healthcare system. Its operating model is concession-based and asset-heavy because the partnership finances and supports the physical infrastructure under a long-term public contract rather than relying on demand-based market revenues. Axium identified CRCHUM as the first phase of the CHUM modernization project and one of the early assets in its Canadian infrastructure fund. Fiera Axium reached financial close on phase 1 in 2010, and the current ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

retiredCompanyBeforeImages.description: CRCHUM is a hospital research center that supports biomedical, clinical, and population health research in Montreal. Its users include researchers, graduate students, fellows, clinicians, and affiliated academic institutions. The operating model is a long-term social infrastructure public-private partnership tied to the delivery and operation of specialized research facilities. Meridiam states that the facility totals about 70,000 square meters and accommodates more than 1,700 people, including around 450 researchers and more than 400 graduate students and postgraduate fellows. The consortium reached commercial and financial close in May 2010, substantial completion in September 2013, and final completion in March 2014. Current public materials do not disclose a current ownership percentage beyond Meridiam's portfolio presentation of the asset.

retiredCompanyBeforeImages.description: CSV Midstream develops, owns, and operates natural gas and NGL processing, compression, and gathering infrastructure in Alberta's Montney region. Its customers are upstream producers that need sour and sweet gas processing, liquids handling, and related takeaway services. The business follows an asset-heavy operating model built around long-lived processing plants and associated field infrastructure, with public materials describing a six-plant platform across northwestern Alberta. Recent company disclosures cite assets including Resthaven, Karr, Pipestone South, Simonette, Valhalla, and the 150 MMcf/d Albright sour gas plant that entered service in 2025. Northleaf infrastructure funds acquired 100% of CSV Midstream in 2019 and supported the concurrent acquisition of the Karr facility, which expanded the company's processing footprint in the basin.
